name: DomainPasswordSpray - Windows PS Spray
description: PowerShell password spray from a Windows domain-joined host. Automatically pulls the user list from AD and respects the domain lockout policy by default. Spray results saved to OutFile. Best used when you already have Windows foothold and domain credentials.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY DOMAINPASSWORDSPRAY ON WINDOWS ===
If you have a Windows domain foothold (workstation, server), you can spray directly
from the machine without sending traffic to a Linux attacker box. The script
automatically queries AD for the user list - no need to build one manually.

=== AUTO USER ENUMERATION + POLICY AWARENESS ===
DomainPasswordSpray automatically:
  1. Queries AD via LDAP for all enabled user accounts
  2. Reads the Fine-Grained Password Policy (or default domain policy)
  3. Stays 2 attempts below lockout threshold by default
This makes it safer than manually spraying without knowing the policy.

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN OUTPUT ===
  [*] Trying password: Spring2022 for user: jsmith
  [+] Found credentials: INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL\jsmith:Spring2022
Valid creds are also written to -OutFile spray_success for later use.

=== PARAMETERS ===
  -Password       → single password to try
  -PasswordList   → file with passwords (sprays each per run, handles timing)
  -UserList       → override auto-enumerated user list with specific file
  -OutFile        → save hits to file
  -Filter         → limit to specific OU or filter (LDAP syntax)

=== CHAIN POSITION ===
This card sits after enumeration (get user list, know the environment) and before
authenticated enumeration. Valid creds from spray enable:
  → Evil-WinRM if target is accessible (TCP 5985)
  → BloodHound collection with the new account
  → Further spraying for admin access
  → CrackMapExec to check Pwn3d! status

=== OPSEC CONSIDERATION ===
Generates 4625 events on the DC per failure. Medium noise - quieter than
manually triggering repeated SMB auth failures, but still generates NTLM
authentication events. AMSI may flag the script if run directly. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication). Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication) - Spray-Passwords.ps1 is used alongside Invoke-DomainPasswordSpray and crackmapexec.

defense.why_it_works: DomainPasswordSpray.ps1 sprays a password across all domain users (auto-pulling the user list and honouring the lockout policy) from a domain host.
defense.prerequisites: A domain user list, candidate password(s), and network access to the auth service.
defense.impact: Compromised domain accounts, gathered while respecting lockout thresholds.
defense.detection: Failed-authentication bursts: Windows 4625 / Kerberos 4771; account lockouts (4740). Spraying = one password across MANY accounts (few failures each - a subtle, distributed pattern). Defender for Identity flags spraying.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4625 OR EventCode=4771)
| stats dc(Account_Name) as accts by Source_Network_Address, bin(_time, 5m)
| where accts>10

index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*Invoke-DomainPasswordSpray*"
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID in (4625, 4771)
| summarize accts=dcount(TargetUserName), attempts=count() by IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where accts > 10
| sort by accts desc
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1110.003 M1032 MFA] MFA defeats spraying; [M1027] strong/unique passwords + [M1036 Account Use Policies] lockout thresholds; alert on distributed failed logons and impossible travel.
defense.evasion: Spray one password low-and-slow with delays to avoid lockouts and volume alerts; rotate source hosts; Kerberos-based spraying avoids 4625.
defense.misconfiguration: The domain's lockout policy is either disabled or set with a threshold high enough (e.g., 10 attempts before lockout) that a low-and-slow spray - one guess per account per 30 minutes - never triggers lockout. Additionally, many accounts share the same simple passwords (company name + year, Season+Year), and the bad-password counter resets after the observation window elapses.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Weak lockout policy (domain default or intentionally lenient):
# Fine-Grained Password Policy:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# LockoutObservationWindow: 00:30:00
# LockoutThreshold:         0          <-- DISABLED! No lockout ever
# OR: LockoutThreshold: 10 (attacker sprays 9 per window, never locks)

# Also: accounts with password = company name:
# Common passwords: Summer2023!, Winter2024!, CompanyName1!
defense.secure_config:
# Set a strong lockout policy:
# Via Default Domain Policy or Fine-Grained Password Policy (PSO):
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local \
    -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutThreshold 5
# LockoutThreshold 5 means 5 bad attempts in 30 min = 30-min lockout

# Fine-Grained PSO for admins (stricter):
New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name AdminPSO \
    -LockoutThreshold 3 -LockoutDuration 01:00:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 01:00:00 \
    -Precedence 1
Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject AdminPSO -Subjects 'Domain Admins'

# Enable Azure AD / Entra ID Password Protection (bans common passwords):
# Also available on-premises via the Azure AD Password Protection agent

# Monitor Event 4740 (Account Locked Out) - spray leaves a cluster of these

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log, PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Sprays a password across the domain from a Windows host, respecting lockout:
  Invoke-DomainPasswordSpray   pulls the user list from AD automatically
  -Password <password>     the single password to spray
  -OutFile spray_success   save hits
  -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue   suppress errors
By default it honors the domain lockout policy so you do not lock accounts; best when you already have a Windows foothold and no Linux box on-segment.
